texto.en: Gaia, Mother Earth, was angry at Zeus and the gods of Olympus.
texto.es: Gaia, Mother Earth, was angry at Zeus and the gods of Olympus.

texto.en: Zeus and the gods had beaten her children, the Titans.
texto.es: Zeus and the gods had beaten her children, the Titans.

texto.en: They had locked the Titans in Tartarus, a deep, dark prison under the earth.
texto.es: They had locked the Titans in Tartarus, a deep, dark prison under the earth.

texto.en: Gaia wanted revenge on the gods.
texto.es: Gaia wanted revenge on the gods.

texto.en: So she decided to raise a new set of children to fight them.
texto.es: So she decided to raise a new set of children to fight them.

texto.en: These new children were the Giants. They were born from the blood of Uranus, the sky god.
texto.es: These new children were the Giants. They were born from the blood of Uranus, the sky god.

texto.en: Long ago, his son Cronus had wounded him, and the blood fell on Gaia, the earth.
texto.es: Long ago, his son Cronus had wounded him, and the blood fell on Gaia, the earth.

texto.en: The Giants were huge and very strong, with long hair and thick beards.
texto.es: The Giants were huge and very strong, with long hair and thick beards.

texto.en: In some tellings, they had snake tails instead of legs.
texto.es: In some tellings, they had snake tails instead of legs.

texto.en: They were born on Phlegra, a smoking plain, and they looked up toward Olympus, the home of the gods.
texto.es: They were born on Phlegra, a smoking plain, and they looked up toward Olympus, the home of the gods.

texto.en: The Giants did not wait long to attack Olympus.

texto.en: They tore up huge rocks and whole mountains, set them on fire, and threw them at the sky.
texto.es: They tore up huge rocks and whole mountains, set them on fire, and threw them at the sky.

texto.en: Rivers changed course, islands sank, and Olympus shook.

texto.en: Zeus, king of the gods, and Ares, god of war, fought back with every weapon.
texto.es: Zeus, king of the gods, and Ares, god of war, fought back with every weapon.

texto.en: But the Giants would not die.

texto.en: An oracle, a priestess who speaks for the gods, told them a secret.
texto.es: An oracle, a priestess who speaks for the gods, told them a secret.

texto.en: The gods could win only with the help of a mortal, a human who can die.
texto.es: The gods could win only with the help of a mortal, a human who can die.

texto.en: Gaia heard it too. She went to find a magic herb that would keep her sons safe, even from a human.
texto.es: Gaia heard it too. She went to find a magic herb that would keep her sons safe, even from a human.

texto.en: So Zeus told Eos the dawn, Selene the moon, and Helios the sun not to shine.
texto.es: So Zeus told Eos the dawn, Selene the moon, and Helios the sun not to shine.

texto.en: In the total darkness, Zeus found the herb first and tore it up by the root.
texto.es: In the total darkness, Zeus found the herb first and tore it up by the root.

texto.en: Athena, goddess of wisdom, went to find that mortal: Heracles, the strongest hero on earth.
texto.es: Athena, goddess of wisdom, went to find that mortal: Heracles, the strongest hero on earth.

texto.en: Heracles came in his lion skin, with his bow. He shot an arrow at the Giant Alcyoneus.
texto.es: Heracles came in his lion skin, with his bow. He shot an arrow at the Giant Alcyoneus.

texto.en: The arrow knocked Alcyoneus down, but he stood up again.

texto.en: He could not die as long as he stayed on the land where he was born.

texto.en: Athena told Heracles to drag him off that land. Heracles did, and Alcyoneus died.

texto.en: Next, Porphyrion, king of the Giants, charged at Hera, queen of the gods, and at Heracles.
texto.es: Next, Porphyrion, king of the Giants, charged at Hera, queen of the gods, and at Heracles.

texto.en: Zeus struck him with a thunderbolt, and Heracles finished him with an arrow.

texto.en: Then the Giant Ephialtes came, huge and furious.

texto.en: So, one by one, a god and a mortal working together brought the Giants down.
